outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Does the edited background, compared with the source, show a recognizable basketball playing area from the visible playing surface and court context, rather than basketball equipment alone?
nodes.criteria: Pass when the visible surface and its markings/context together identify a basketball playing area; fail when the assessable background shows only equipment or a generic surface without recognizable court context; unknown only when the relevant background cannot be assessed. Do not require a full regulation layout or prominent markings if the scene otherwise clearly reads as a court.
nodes.binding: Compare the edited background with the source to assess the requested background replacement. Judge the background scene, not the unchanged foreground person. Consider the visible floor and markings together with basketball context; a hoop or balls alone are insufficient. Report the visible evidence rather than relying on another support's status.

nodes.question: Does the edited background contain visible evidence that the playing surface and markings belong to a recognizable basketball-court setting, rather than merely showing basketball equipment or generic lines?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the visible playing surface and markings, considered with the basketball context, support a recognizable court setting; fail if assessable evidence is limited to isolated equipment, a generic surface, or non-identifying lines; unknown if the relevant background details cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited background relative to the source. Assess the relationship of the floor, curved/straight markings, and basketball equipment as evidence about the background, not as a completion verdict. Do not treat any single line or equipment alone as conclusive.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Complete (yes) if the supports together establish that the source background has been replaced by a recognizable basketball-court setting; court context may be established by the visible playing surface/lines together with basketball equipment, and neither a single support report nor a disagreement alone is decisive. Partial if there is evidenced basketball-related background progress but the background is not recognizably a court. Absent (no) if there is no visible requested progress. Unknown if the saved evidence cannot resolve whether requested progress occurred; do not convert conflicting reports or uncertainty into a fabricated failure or completion. Unchanged foreground subject matter is irrelevant.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
